recurrent_mechanisms.mechanism: Across all four groups, the T1 route fails to develop far enough to expose a supported semantic/adoption/action chain.
Long horizons are explained by interface/role-activation nondevelopment rather than by CPR persistence.

divergence_patterns: G2 is dominated by repeated invalid action-envelope rejection; G3–G5 retain the requirement but do not form a material version-review/repair chain.
The precise runtime failure mode varies, but all four trajectories leave the repository unchanged and fail before retrospective state can generate a downstream C/P effect.
boundary_interpretation: This cohort is evidence about observability limits, not evidence that historical-process mechanisms cannot occur in MetaGPT generally.
A 64-turn trajectory is not itself Dynamic R; R requires historical state to regain authority and generate a later C/P effect.
cross_group_semantic_synthesis.cohort_conclusion: MetaGPT X2-T1 is a consistent process-surface negative cohort. All four frozen runs terminate at framework/interface nondevelopment boundaries before a version-review mechanism can mature. The repeated absence of CPR therefore constrains what was observed in this implementation/task path, while preventing the study from misclassifying long nonproductive execution as temporal permission penetration.

constraints: Cell-level Layer-C verdicts are sealed and are not modified by cohort synthesis.
Boundary-excluded natural cells remain excluded rather than imputed.
Dimension recurrence is descriptive across frozen stochastic realizations; it is not a rerun-based reproducibility claim.
